introduction_markdown: CAMEROON GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination, June 2020, Ordinary Level, Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL QUESTIONS IN SECTION A and ANY TWO QUESTIONS FROM EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. IN SECTIONS B AND C, ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C but NOT a combination of all three. Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory, answer all questions). Section B: Mechanics (if this section is chosen, then Section C may not be chosen; answer any two questions). Section C: Statistics and Probability (if this section is chosen, then Section B may not be chosen; answer any two questions). All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2. Formulae Booklets may be used.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The points P and Q have position vectors $3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}$ and $2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}$ respectively.

(a) Write down vector equation of the line $l_1$ passing through the points P and Q in the form $\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{a}+t\mathbf{b}$, where $t$ is a scalar. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Direction of the line: $\overrightarrow{PQ}=\mathbf{q}-\mathbf{p}=(2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})-(3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})=-\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$.

Take $\mathbf{a}=\mathbf{p}$ (a point on the line) and $\mathbf{b}=-\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$:

**$l_1:\ \mathbf{r}=(3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})+t(-\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j})$.**

(Any equivalent form is accepted, for example $\mathbf{r}=2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+t(\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j})$.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Another line $l_2$, has vector equation $l_2:\ \mathbf{r}=3\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+s(\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})$, where $s$ is a scalar.

Find,

(b) the position vector of the point of intersection of the lines $l_1$ and $l_2$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A point on $l_1$ is $(3-t)\mathbf{i}+(-2+3t)\mathbf{j}$ and a point on $l_2$ is $(3+s)\mathbf{i}+(3+2s)\mathbf{j}$. At the intersection the components are equal:

$$\mathbf{i}:\ 3-t=3+s\ \Longrightarrow\ s=-t,$$

$$\mathbf{j}:\ -2+3t=3+2s=3-2t\ \Longrightarrow\ 5t=5\ \Longrightarrow\ t=1,\ s=-1.$$

Position vector: with $t=1$ on $l_1$: $(3-1)\mathbf{i}+(-2+3)\mathbf{j}=2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}$. Check with $s=-1$ on $l_2$: $(3-1)\mathbf{i}+(3-2)\mathbf{j}=2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}$.

**The lines meet at the point with position vector $2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}$** (this is the point Q).

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) the cosine of the angle between the lines $l_1$ and $l_2$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The angle between the lines is the angle between their direction vectors $\mathbf{d}_1=-\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{d}_2=\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}$.

$$\mathbf{d}_1\cdot\mathbf{d}_2=(-1)(1)+(3)(2)=5,\qquad|\mathbf{d}_1|=\sqrt{10},\qquad|\mathbf{d}_2|=\sqrt5.$$

$$\cos\theta=\frac{\mathbf{d}_1\cdot\mathbf{d}_2}{|\mathbf{d}_1||\mathbf{d}_2|}=\frac{5}{\sqrt{10}\sqrt5}=\frac{5}{\sqrt{50}}=\frac{5}{5\sqrt2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}.$$

**$\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\approx0.707$** (the angle between the lines is $45^\circ$).
